title: Hilbert's 3rd Problem: the Tensor-Product Dehn Invariant Group
description: A genuine Mathlib `TensorProduct` construction of the Dehn invariant target group D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ / πℚ), replacing the parent entry's crude list surrogate. Two facts that carry the whole geometric argument are proved rigorously: rational multiples of π vanish (so the cube — and every rational-angle polyhedron — has Dehn invariant 0), and supplementary angles cancel, l ⊗ θ + l ⊗ (π − θ) = 0 — the algebraic heart of 'cutting preserves the Dehn invariant', which the parent could only state as `:= trivial`. Axiom-free and sorry-free. Does NOT claim the full Sydler completeness theorem.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's Third Problem (1900) asks whether two polyhedra of equal volume are always scissors congruent. Max Dehn answered no the same year by introducing the Dehn invariant, an element of ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℚ) summing length ⊗ (dihedral angle) over edges: it is preserved under scissors congruence, yet the cube (angles π/2) gives 0 while the regular tetrahedron (angle arccos(1/3)) does not. In 1965 Sydler proved the deep converse: volume together with the Dehn invariant is a complete invariant. The parent gallery entry `hilbert-3` formalizes Dehn's obstruction but models the invariant with a list-of-pairs surrogate and leaves the structural lemmas `cutting_preserves_dehn` and `isometry_preserves_dehn` as `:= trivial`. Its open question OQ-02 asks to formalize Sydler's theorem via Mathlib's tensor-product machinery.
overview.problemStatement: Open question OQ-02 asks to build the Dehn invariant inside genuine tensor-product machinery (toward Sydler's completeness theorem). Sydler's full 1965 theorem rests on transcendence theory and a hard surjectivity ('if') direction and is out of reach of a single session; this entry deliberately does not claim it. Instead it constructs the actual target group D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ / πℚ) with Mathlib's `TensorProduct` and proves the algebraic facts on which both Dehn's obstruction and Sydler's theorem are phrased.
overview.text: The Dehn invariant lives in D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ / πℚ). Tensoring a length with a rational multiple of π gives 0, and supplementary angles cancel: l ⊗ θ + l ⊗ (π − θ) = 0.
overview.proofStrategy: The angle group A = ℝ / πℚ is the quotient of ℝ by the subgroup πℚ, realized as the range of the additive homomorphism q ↦ q·π : ℚ →+ ℝ. The class map angleClass = QuotientAddGroup.mk' is additive, and an angle q·π is 0 in A by `QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff`. The Dehn target group is D = ℝ ⊗[ℤ] A and a single edge contributes dehnTerm l θ = l ⊗ₜ angleClass θ. Rational-angle vanishing is then `angleClass_eq_zero_of_ratPi` followed by `TensorProduct.tmul_zero`; additivity in length and angle are `TensorProduct.add_tmul` / `tmul_add`; and supplementary-angle cancellation follows from angleClass(θ) + angleClass(π−θ) = angleClass(π) = 0 via `tmul_add` and `tmul_zero`. The whole-polyhedron Dehn invariant is a Finset.sum of edge terms, and `Finset.sum_eq_zero` gives D = 0 whenever every dihedral angle is a rational multiple of π — specializing to angle π/2 yields the cube.
keyInsights: **The honest target group, not a surrogate**: D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℚ) is built with Mathlib's real `TensorProduct`, so the Dehn invariant is an element of an actual abelian group with genuine bilinearity — the structure Sydler's theorem is a statement about — rather than the parent's list-of-pairs with an ad-hoc `isZero` predicate

**Rational angles vanish for the right reason**: l ⊗ (q·π) = 0 because the *angle class* q·π is literally 0 in ℝ/πℚ (a quotient computation), after which `tmul_zero` finishes — this is the exact mechanism making D(cube) = 0 and, more generally, making every rational-angle polyhedron (e.g. the 2D Bolyai–Gerwien world) Dehn-trivial

**Supplementary cancellation is the cutting lemma**: a planar cut through an edge of dihedral angle θ replaces it with angles θ and π−θ on the two new pieces; l ⊗ θ + l ⊗ (π−θ) = l ⊗ π = 0 because θ + (π−θ) = π ≡ 0 in ℝ/πℚ — this single tensor identity is why cutting preserves the Dehn invariant, replacing the parent's `cutting_preserves_dehn := trivial`

**Bilinearity replaces hand-waving**: additivity in length (`add_tmul`) and in angle (`tmul_add`) are now theorems of the construction, not informal remarks, giving the Dehn invariant the additive-functional structure required to even state the scissors-congruence homomorphism

**Scope honesty**: this is the tensor-product *foundation* toward Sydler, not Sydler. The tetrahedron's nonvanishing (Niven's transcendence theorem) and the hard 'if' direction of Sydler are explicitly out of scope and not assumed here
prerequisites: Tensor product of ℤ-modules (abelian groups): M ⊗_ℤ N and the simple tensor m ⊗ₜ n
Bilinearity of the tensor product: add_tmul, tmul_add, tmul_zero
Quotient of an abelian group by a subgroup: ℝ / πℚ and QuotientAddGroup.mk'
Range of an additive homomorphism as a subgroup, and eq_zero_iff for the quotient
The Dehn invariant Σ length ⊗ (dihedral angle) and its role in Hilbert's Third Problem

conclusion.summary: This entry grounds the Dehn invariant in Mathlib's genuine tensor-product machinery, constructing the target group D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ / πℚ) and proving the two algebraic facts that carry Dehn's obstruction: rational multiples of π vanish (`dehnTerm_eq_zero_of_ratPi`), so the cube and every rational-angle polyhedron have Dehn invariant 0 (`cube_dehnSum_zero`, `dehnSum_eq_zero_of_ratPi`); and supplementary angles cancel (`dehnTerm_supplementary`), the algebraic heart of cutting-invariance that the parent left as `:= trivial`. Additivity in length and angle are also derived. All results are axiom-free and sorry-free (verified via `#print axioms`: only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound).
conclusion.implications: Replacing the parent's list surrogate with the real group ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℚ) puts the Dehn invariant on the footing Sydler's completeness theorem actually requires, and turns two previously-`trivial` placeholders into honest tensor identities. The supplementary-angle cancellation is exactly the local computation behind 'cutting preserves the Dehn invariant', so this is genuine progress on the structural half of OQ-02, even though the full Sydler theorem remains open.
openQuestions: Prove the tetrahedron's Dehn term is nonzero in D: with l ≠ 0 and angleClass(arccos(1/3)) ≠ 0, show l ⊗ angleClass(arccos(1/3)) ≠ 0 by exhibiting a ℚ-linear functional on ℝ/πℚ separating the coset (using that ℝ and ℝ/πℚ are ℚ-vector spaces, so ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℚ) ≅ ℝ ⊗_ℚ (ℝ/πℚ) has nonvanishing simple tensors) — this needs Niven's theorem only to know the coset is nonzero

Assemble cutting-invariance: define a dissection of a polyhedron and prove the sum of pieces' Dehn invariants equals the whole, with internal cut edges cancelling via `dehnTerm_supplementary`, upgrading the parent's `cutting_preserves_dehn := trivial` to a real theorem

Formalize the Dehn invariant as an additive homomorphism on a scissors-congruence group, the homomorphism whose kernel Sydler's 'if' direction controls — the entry point to the full completeness theorem

mainTheorems.name: dehnTerm_eq_zero_of_ratPi
mainTheorems.description: Rational-angle vanishing: a length tensored with a rational multiple of π is 0 in D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/πℚ) — the algebraic reason D(cube) = 0
mainTheorems.leanType: (l θ : ℝ) (q : ℚ) → θ = q * Real.pi → dehnTerm l θ = 0

mainTheorems.name: dehnTerm_supplementary
mainTheorems.description: Supplementary-angle cancellation: l ⊗ θ + l ⊗ (π − θ) = 0, the algebraic heart of 'cutting preserves the Dehn invariant'
mainTheorems.leanType: (l θ : ℝ) → dehnTerm l θ + dehnTerm l (Real.pi - θ) = 0

mainTheorems.name: cube_dehnSum_zero
mainTheorems.description: The cube has Dehn invariant 0 in the genuine tensor-product group: every edge carries dihedral angle π/2 = (1/2)·π
mainTheorems.leanType: (s : Finset ι) (len : ι → ℝ) → dehnSum s len (fun _ => Real.pi / 2) = 0

mainTheorems.name: dehnSum_eq_zero_of_ratPi
mainTheorems.description: A polyhedron all of whose dihedral angles are rational multiples of π has Dehn invariant 0
mainTheorems.leanType: (s : Finset ι) (len ang : ι → ℝ) → (∀ i ∈ s, ∃ q : ℚ, ang i = q * Real.pi) → dehnSum s len ang = 0

mainTheorems.name: dehnTerm_add_angle
mainTheorems.description: Additivity of the Dehn term in the angle: l ⊗ (θ₁ + θ₂) = l ⊗ θ₁ + l ⊗ θ₂
mainTheorems.leanType: (l θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ) → dehnTerm l (θ₁ + θ₂) = dehnTerm l θ₁ + dehnTerm l θ₂

mainTheorems.name: angleClass_eq_zero_of_ratPi
mainTheorems.description: An angle that is a rational multiple of π is 0 in the angle group A = ℝ / πℚ
mainTheorems.leanType: (θ : ℝ) (q : ℚ) → θ = q * Real.pi → angleClass θ = 0

originalContributions: Constructs the genuine Dehn invariant target group D = ℝ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ / πℚ) with Mathlib's real `TensorProduct`, replacing the parent entry's list-of-pairs surrogate and its ad-hoc `isZero` predicate

`dehnTerm_eq_zero_of_ratPi`: rigorous proof that a length tensored with a rational multiple of π is 0 in D — the actual algebraic mechanism behind D(cube) = 0, where the parent merely defined `isZero` to assert it

`dehnTerm_supplementary`: l ⊗ θ + l ⊗ (π − θ) = 0, the supplementary-angle cancellation that is the algebraic heart of 'cutting preserves the Dehn invariant'; the parent left the corresponding statement as `cutting_preserves_dehn := trivial`
Additivity of the Dehn term in both length (`dehnTerm_add_length`, via `add_tmul`) and angle (`dehnTerm_add_angle`, via `tmul_add`), giving the invariant its honest bilinear structure

`dehnSum_eq_zero_of_ratPi` and `cube_dehnSum_zero`: the whole-polyhedron Dehn invariant vanishes for any polyhedron with all dihedral angles rational multiples of π, recovering Dehn's cube computation inside the real tensor-product group

The file is self-contained and Mathlib-only. Scope is honest: this entry builds the genuine tensor-product Dehn invariant group and proves the rational-angle and supplementary-angle facts toward Sydler's theorem; it does NOT prove Sydler's completeness theorem, nor the regular tetrahedron's Dehn nonvanishing (which requires Niven's transcendence theorem). Those remain open and are listed as open questions.
